messages:
incident-bot: :warning: HIGH-PRIORITY — Observed sustained 99th-pct tail latency increase across text-generation endpoints in prod-usw2 starting ~5m ago. Error-rate stable but throughput dropped due to long-running token streams. Auto-escalating to #incidents.

maya (oncall): saw it. dashboards show streaming workers pegged and queues backing up. CPU/GPU utilization high on a subset of hosts. Not sure if it's a single model or broad.

eli (sre): confirming. It looks correlated with long-lived SSE connections. Token service latency spikes when concurrency of streaming sessions > 2k. We have active autoscaler but it can't spin up thumb-sized workers fast enough.

zoe (prod-eng): any recent rollout? model or runtime? I don't see a dedicated deploy in last 30m. Could be client-side pattern change holding streams open.

maya (oncall): no deploy. I'm going to follow the streaming-mitigation runbook: step 1 — limit stream concurrency then step 2 — disable streaming responses if needed. Proposing temporary streaming suppression for prod-usw2 to stabilize throughput. :point_up:

sam (support): if we disable streaming, customers using SSE/streaming SDK will see degraded UX. Need a support blurb prepared. Any estimate on duration?

eli (sre): aiming for 15-30m for mitigation + stabilization. We'll monitor metrics and then selectively re-enable. Action plan: (1) Apply rate limit on streaming routes to 1 req/sec per token-stream client id, (2) flip streaming feature flag to OFF for prod-usw2, (3) shift long-poll fallback to regular chunked responses. Doing (1) now.

eli (sre): Applied temporary rate-limit rule: `route: /v1/streaming/* -> concurrency=1 per-key, burst=2, window=60s`. Seeing small improvement but still high tail due to existing sessions.

maya (oncall): executing feature flag toggle now: `/infra/feature-toggle streaming_responses --env=prod-usw2 --state=off --reason="latency mitigation"`. Will post when done.

incident-bot: Feature toggle request queued. Approvers: zoe, ryan.

zoe (prod-eng): approving, go ahead.

ryan (oncall-2): approving as backup.

maya (oncall): Toggle complete. streaming_responses = OFF for prod-usw2. Patch applied to edge layer, ingress returning 202 + Retry-After for new streaming requests. Old SSE connections will be allowed to drain (grace period = 120s).

eli (sre): immediate telemetry: accepted request rate back to normal, average token latency dropping. Queues draining. Spike in short polling calls observed (clients falling back). Keep watching error budget and latency.

sam (support): drafting customer message now: "We're temporarily disabling streaming responses in US-WEST-2 to stabilize latency. Your requests will return full responses or chunked fallback; streaming will be re-enabled as soon as it's safe. Expected window 15-30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption." Will post to status and paging channels after we confirm stabilization.

maya (oncall): handing off to ryan for overnight watch. Key follow-ups: (a) investigate why streaming sessions hold resources (KV cache retention), (b) evaluate faster drain / connection termination policy, (c) postmortem if >1h. Handoff notes: tags, dashboards, runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/streaming-mitigation

ryan (oncall-2): acked. I'll monitor for next 3 hours and coordinate re-enable with prod-eng. If we see requeueing or error-rate >0.5% revert to rate-limited streaming instead of full off.

zoe (prod-eng): plan for next hour: instrument more granular GC of KV cache for streams and add metrics to trace long-lived connections by client-id. Also prepare a canary re-enable: start with 1% traffic to streaming after queues stable.

eli (sre): metrics at T+8m after toggle: 95th latency down 35%, 99th down 48%, queue depth reduced ~80%. Looks good.

maya (oncall): great. sam, please file a short status update on status.redwood.ai with the support blurb and indicate engineering mitigation in progress.

sam (support): posted status update and emailed top 20 paying customers flagged as streaming-heavy. Template used: `We have temporarily disabled streaming in US-WEST-2 to stabilize token generation latency. ETA 15-30m. Contact support@redwood.ai for urgent needs.`

ryan (oncall-2): I'll be the re-enable owner. Plan: wait 20m, run canary at 0.5% traffic, observe 10m, then ramp to 1%/5%/full if stable. Will coordinate with zoe before each increase.

maya (oncall): adding follow-up ticket: INC-176800-STREAMING-DEEP-DIVE assigned to prod-eng with due: 72h.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied (streaming disabled prod-usw2). Pager routing: ryan (oncall-2) now responsible. Please update thread with any customer escalations.

eli (sre): noting ephemeral config we toggled: `edge::feature.streaming_responses=off`, rate-limits persisted separately. Will commit remediation notes to runbook.

zoe (prod-eng): filing PR for longer-term fix: better KV eviction heuristics and connection accounting. Will link PR here once created.

maya (oncall): closing primary alert. Monitoring continues and we'll reopen if regressions appear. Thanks everyone. :handshake:

ryan (oncall-2): monitoring, will post re-enable progress in this thread.

sam (support): closing customer comms loop for now unless we get replies.
